target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The complete selected original text is identical within the same SEC Item after removing line-leading bullet formatting and normalizing whitespace. Neither LLM agent was used for this link.

Both disclosures address the risk that government actions, export regulations, tariffs, and trade restrictions limit the company's ability to export products. The 2023 disclosure broadly states government actions may limit exports. The 2024 disclosure expands on this by specifying export regulations (EAR/ITAR), tariffs, and trade protection measures as the mechanisms limiting exports, citing specific sentences on export control restrictions and their impact on sales and forecasting.

comparisons.peer_topic: Export Control and Government Regulation Compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: The company is subject to complex domestic and international laws, including U.S. Export Administration Regulations, which may require significant compliance expenses. U.S. government restrictions on entities and technologies, along with potential retaliatory actions by other governments, could limit business with certain customers or suppliers and adversely affect revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose that government export controls and regulations restrict their ability to sell products to certain customers, potentially harming revenue. AMD states broadly that 'Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.' Broadcom provides more specificity, noting that 'The U.S. government may continue to add companies to its restricted entity list... which have had and may in the future have an adverse effect on our revenue' and that these measures 'will likely limit or prevent us from doing business with certain of our customers or suppliers'.

sentences.text: ◦Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.

The U.S. government may continue to add companies to its restricted entity list and/or technologies to its list of prohibited exports to specific countries, which have had and may in the future have an adverse effect on our revenue and our ability to sell our products.

These restrictive governmental actions and any similar measures that may be imposed on U.S. companies by other governments, especially in light of ongoing trade tensions with China, will likely limit or prevent us from doing business with certain of our customers or suppliers and harm our ability to compete effectively or otherwise negatively affect our ability to sell our products.

peer_results.rationale: Intel's candidate disclosures focus on risks related to government customer sales (budgetary cycles, procurement laws) and general compliance with complex evolving laws (data privacy, 5G, IP). None of the cited sentences specifically address export control regulations limiting the ability to export products to certain foreign customers, which is the specific topic of AMD's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks from international trade disputes and export restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: International trade disputes, geopolitical tensions, and protectionism may lead to increased export restrictions, tariffs, and trade barriers that can raise manufacturing costs, limit market access, restrict component procurement, and impede operations, with geopolitical tensions specifically risking export controls on AI-enabled products.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and AMD both identify government export restrictions as a risk that limits the ability to sell to specific customers or markets. Micron's disclosure is more expansive, linking this to trade disputes and geopolitical tensions, stating 'Government actions and regulations, such as export restrictions, tariffs, and trade protection measures, may limit our ability to sell our products to certain customers or markets, or could otherwise restrict our ability to conduct operations.' AMD's disclosure is a concise, direct statement on the same core risk: 'Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.'

sentences.text: ◦Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.

Government actions and regulations, such as export restrictions, tariffs, and trade protection measures, may limit our ability to sell our products to certain customers or markets, or could otherwise restrict our ability to conduct operations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks of future and expanded export control changes
comparisons.peer_summary: The USG may change export control rules at any time, potentially restricting further products, limiting GPU cluster usage, or extending controls to gaming GPUs and networking products, which could disrupt supply chains, disadvantage NVIDIA, and encourage customers to design-out US semiconductors.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose that US government export control rules can change and restrict specific products, negatively impacting business. AMD highlights the general limitation on exports: 'Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.' NVIDIA specifics this with regard to AI and geopolitical tensions, noting 'the USG has changed and may again change the export control rules at any time and further subject a wider range of our products to export restrictions and licensing requirements, negatively impacting our business and financial results.'

sentences.text: ◦Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.

Given the increasing strategic importance of AI and rising geopolitical tensions, the USG has changed and may again change the export control rules at any time and further subject a wider range of our products to export restrictions and licensing requirements, negatively impacting our business and financial results.

comparisons.peer_summary: Political actions by governments, particularly regarding trade and national security, could limit business with certain customers or suppliers, potentially advantaging competitors through increased sales or technology transfer.
comparisons.comparison: Qualcomm and AMD both identify political and trade policy actions by governments as risks that limit business with certain customers. AMD states 'Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.' Qualcomm expands on this by specifying the mechanism: 'political actions, including trade and/or national security protection policies, or other actions by governments, particularly the U.S. and Chinese governments... could in the future limit or prevent us from transacting business with certain of our customers or suppliers'.

sentences.text: ◦Government actions and regulations may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers.

Further, political actions, including trade and/or national security protection policies, or other actions by governments, particularly the U.S. and Chinese governments, have in the past, currently are and could in the future limit or prevent us from transacting business with certain of our customers or suppliers; limit, prevent or discourage certain of our customers or suppliers from transacting business with us; or make it more expensive to do so.
